NEITHER

Speed is a measure of distance over time.
20 km/h is 20 km/h, regardless of the vehicle.

traffic Reality Check

But in the city,
context is king.

While 20km/h is mathematically identical, average travel speeds in cities tell a different story. Cars face congestion, lights, and parking delays. Bicycles often maintain a steadier pace or filter through traffic.

The Cost of Speed

Even if speed is equal, the energy required to maintain it is vastly different.
Physics favors the bicycle.

directions_car

Car at 20 km/h

Rolling Resistance + Drag

~207 N Force Required
9.4x More Force
pedal_bike

Cyclist at 20 km/h

Rolling Resistance + Drag

~22 N Force Required
1x

lightbulb Why so different?

  • check_circle Mass: A car weighs ~1500kg vs a bike+rider ~85kg. Moving 1.5 tons takes significantly more energy, even at low speeds.
  • check_circle Rolling Resistance: Car tires are wide and deformed by massive weight, creating ~187N of resistance vs just ~4N for thin bike tires.
  • check_circle Efficiency: A bicycle is the most energy-efficient mode of transport ever invented.
